item.base_system: Random HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy (bcc structure, 128,000 atoms)
item.intervention: Evolution of the random sample using Metropolis Monte Carlo (Kawasaki-type swaps) to induce chemical short-range order (SRO)
item.processing: Metropolis MC with 100 K rejection factor, 10 swaps attempted per step, run for 4.7e6 steps
item.test_conditions: Temperature 300 K (after relaxation from 10 mK), periodic boundary conditions
item.structure_change: Formation of HfTi and TiZr clusters ordered in B2 structure; reduction in lattice distortion (mean atomic displacement decreased from 0.0173 nm to 0.0153 nm)
item.property_change: Lattice heat conductivity increased by around 12% compared to the random alloy
item.attributed_mechanism: Increase of conductivity alongside SRO cluster percolation pathways, despite expectations of reduced scattering times
quotes: With increasing SRO, a tendency of forming HfTi and TiZr clusters is found.
SRO reduces the lattice distortion thanks to the formation of the B2 ordered structures and, therefore, this would help increasing the thermal conductivity.
due to the increase of the conductivity alongside SRO cluster percolation pathways, SRO increases the lattice heat conductivity by around 12 %.

item.base_system: Random HfNbTaTiZr alloy
item.intervention: Increasing the number of Monte Carlo steps to increase the degree of chemical SRO
item.processing: Kawasaki MC simulation evolving the system from random to equilibrium states over 4.7e6 steps
item.test_conditions: Canonical ensemble at 100 K for MC evolution, analyzed at 300 K
item.structure_change: Development of B2 structures for HfTi and TiZr pairs; percolation of HfTi clusters occurs slightly before 1e5 MC steps
